title: Student's Self-Efficacy and Perceptions of Online Learning on the Use Learning Management System
reason: Re-extraction only (inclusion not re-decided). Full text shows a questionnaire-only SEM study: no LMS log data. The 'indicators' are self-efficacy items. On the full-text rules this record would fail I1-I4 (NOREL); flagged for adjudication.

extraction.n_quote: We sent a questionnaire to 400 students and received 155 students with complete responses.
extraction.population: Madrasah Ibtidaiyah teacher-education students, semesters 4 and 6, 1 institute
extraction.lms_indicators: none recorded by the LMS; self-reported self-efficacy items about LMS use (e.g. 'I manage to finish all the online activities, such as discussions, assignments and quizzes', 'I can send the assignments online')
extraction.outcome_or_construct: self-reported perceptions of online learning (impact, comfort, teacher support); self-efficacy factors F1-F5
extraction.notes: Reported paths (self-report ↔ self-report, not indicator-outcome, so not entered as effect sizes): path coefficient 0.519 (self-efficacy to complete online courses (F1, self-report) ↔ perceived impact (self-report); quote: 'F1 --> Impact 0.519 0.000', Table 6, p. 168); path coefficient 0.419 (self-efficacy to complete online courses (F1) ↔ perceived comfort; quote: 'F1 --> Comfort 0.419 0.004', Table 6, p. 168); path coefficient 0.357 (self-efficacy for handling LMS tools (F5) ↔ perceived teacher support; quote: 'F5 --> Support 0.357 0.001', Table 6, p. 168). Table 2 row is wrong on two cells: design is not 'Survey + log analysis' (no log, trace or LMS record is analysed anywhere; data are Google-Forms questionnaires), and the listed LMS-side indicators are questionnaire items, not platform measures. n: abstract says 'collect data from 156 students'; method says 155 complete responses. Five of 11 hypothesised paths non-significant (Table 6). F4 Cronbach alpha 0.478, AVE 0.3 (Table 2).

table2_current.lms_indicators: Course and assignment completion, discussion participation, test passing
